   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  May 11, 2023
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  May 2, 2023
Subject:  Recreation Program Report - 3rd Quarter Review FY 2022/23

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary: This report covers recreation programs held during the second quarter of
fiscal year 2022-2023. During these months there is typically less interest in programs due to
the weather and time change.

Fitness
It has now been over 3 months since we switched over to Civic Rec and began
rebuilding our membership base. We had a very strong showing with 2,580
memberships sold in our 3rd quarter. Of the 2,580, our Fitness memberships accounted
for 1,925 of the totals, making it our most popular membership.

Our Personal Training program has seen a slight change in preference. It appears that
Private sessions are becoming more popular than the Semi-Private option. Typically,
winter is our slowest season, but you would not be able to tell given that we completed
140 hours.

Lastly, we have rebuilt our Group Exercise class schedule after losing some instructors
due to Covid closures and restrictions. We now offer 28 classes to a variety of
populations that include youth and seniors.

Aquatics:
Winter doesn’t slow down at the Patricia G. Mitchell Swim Stadium due to it being one
of the only indoor, Olympic-sized heated pools in the area that is open year-round. Our
traditional Learn-to-Swim program takes a break, but the slowing of the season allows
us to introduce special programs and participate in special events. In January, the
Swim Stadium participated in the Sports Center’s Open House where we showcased
current/future programs and offered free entry into Family Swim. We also featured a
booth during the City’s Centennial Event where we promoted our programs and served
as the official First Aid Booth.

Pre-Competitive Swim Class, a winter favorite, resumed in January and goes through
March. It is currently our best feeder program for our partner organization South Gate

  3
 Aquatics Club. The Aquatics Team also hosted the 10th annual Swim Clinic in
February, which is a special program designed for competitive swimmers ages 5-18
looking to improve technique, build endurance, and enhance speed.

In February, our Lifeguarding Instructors held 3 different Adult and Pediatric First
Aid/CPR/AED courses, where we certified almost 30 staff and community members in
important, life-saving skills. In March, we hosted Special Olympics’ Swimming Coaches
Camp and presented our annual Lifeguard Class, which trains participants in American
Red Cross Lifeguarding/First Aid/CPR/AED and is our biggest hiring push for new
lifeguards. We also hosted 6 swim meets during the winter session: 4 South Central
Swim League meets, which bring approximately 6 local teams, 400 local swimmers, and
900 spectators per meet, and 2 USA Swimming Meets hosted by our partner
organization South Gate Aquatics Club. The month of March not only marks the
beginning of our spring season, but the return of our most popular program – swim
lessons for all ages and levels! We are currently offering group, private and semi-
private swim lessons, and have over 300 registrants for this month.

Youth Sports:
Winter classes were conducted and even through all the rainouts, classes were able to
complete all 9 sessions. Winter registration is typically lower due to weather and
temperature, but our registrants were consistent and showed up each week ready to
learn and participate. Youth Sports staff are currently working on the curriculum and
drills for our Upcoming Basketball All-Star Skills Challenge on 5/22. This event is open
to children aged 7-12 and will test their ball handling, passing, shooting, and agility
skills.

Adult Sports:
Our Fall Adult Softball Leagues are currently in season and trying to conclude. This
season has been delayed tremendously due to the consistent rainouts. We have 12
Men’s teams registered for Thursday evenings (2 divisions) and 17 Co-ed teams
registered for Friday evenings (3 divisions). 1st place winners in each of their respective
divisions of the Fall season will be awarded Championship Hoodies. 2nd place winners
of each division will be awarded an insulated water bottle. Our Men’s Spring Basketball
season has begun with six brand new teams to the league. The competition is stacked
and evenly matched with very competitive games. Open play volleyball continues to be
one of the most popular nights during the week, this quarter saw a rise in numbers and
ended with a total of 646 drop-in participants.

Partner Organizations (Sports):
SG Aztecs pre-season football and cheer practices have commenced at Hollydale
Regional Park. The Aztecs are working hard and looking forward to a successful 2023-
24 season.

SGJAA Winter Basketball Season has concluded; teams faced off in 4 divisions and
concluded with All-Star games and practices for the top players in their respective
divisions. At the end of the JAA basketball season our traditional Staff vs Coaches

  4
 game took place, we had more than 100 spectators in attendance to cheer or jeer their
teams. The JAA coaches were successful this season and defeated our team, but we
will get our shot at redemption in the Summer. JAA Spring Baseball & Softball are
currently conducting clinics and the Spring Season is set to begin on Opening Day on
Saturday, May 6 at 10am.

Social Media:
Our total followers are now up to 3,666. In the last quarter we had 14 posts, 109
stories, and 1 reel. We are currently in the recruitment process for a Recreation
Marketing Coordinator to oversee the Social Media Task Force.

Contract Classes:
Most of the Dance Classes were full to capacity. Mexican Folk had to open another
class since there were 10 on the waitlist and the instructor wanted to accommodate
them. Teen Hip Hop, Teen Art Club and Teen Comics were all canceled due to low or
no enrollments.

Youth Classes:
Tot Time registration increased a little, instead of having 12-15 in classes we had 15-17
register. Tiny Two’s were all full. There is a Spring trip planned to the Long Beach
Aquarium, since registrations increased.

Cultural Arts:
With the Centennial Celebration happening on January 20, 2023, the Museum hosted
the collection of some of the items from the Time Capsule for display. Items were
viewed by the public during the Celebration as well as Tuesdays 10 am – 1 pm and
Thursdays 3:30 – 5:30 pm and Saturdays 1-5 pm. There was also an Art Exhibit on
display, “Mi Barrio/My Neighborhood”. The Art Club 7-12 yrs., Adult Oil Painting and
Watercolor Painting classes were all full. There was also a Women’s History Mart on
March 25 that was attended by many from the community. They also hosted a variety of
Narrative Poetry workshops throughout the months of February and March.

Special Events:
Centennial Ceremony: Recreation staff was responsible for the lineup of the Community
performances from local talent, High School marching Band, and the performances
from the Mariachis, Mariachi Espectacular, and the live band, Here 4 Now. Staff were
also responsible for the decorations for the stage and throughout the festival set up. The
decorations were used for Council’s cover picture for the Spring Connect. Staff
purchased and distributed 1,500 glow items to all attendees to enhance the viewing of
the Fireworks show.

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  May 11, 2023
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Glenn Massey, Parks Superintendent
Date:  May 2, 2023
Subject:  Grounds and Facility Maintenance 3rd Quarter Report FY 2022/23

Recommended Motion: Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary: For the Commission’s consideration and review; the following are
details of both Grounds and Facility Maintenance updates for this past quarter.

Grounds Maintenance
 Staff has continued routine procedures such as, pressure washing picnic tables,
 benches, playground areas, handball courts, small quad, bandstand, outside restrooms,
 golf course, senior center, City Hall and other areas as needed, and in preparation for
 rentals.

 We are continuing to over-seed high traffic areas with summer blend seed to fill in bare
 spots and thicken the grass to make it more pleasant for patrons; also, daily fixing
 irrigation issues that pop up throughout all City parks and City Hall.

 Since spring started the gopher activity throughout all City Parks has increased, Staff
 works daily on eradicating them.

 We purchased replacement plants for the planters around the auditorium. Six flats of
 Gazanias were planted in the raised planter in front of the Auditorium and 20 Indian
 Hawthorne were purchased to replace those that have died or been stolen. These were
 planted around the Auditorium.

 On Saturday, April 22 the Tree People organization planted 30 trees on the south side
 of South Gate Park; Tipu, Ash, and Fern Pine to name a few species.

 Four twenty-four-inch box size Fern Pines were planted in the Cook House area.

 Staff continue servicing and beautifying over 180 acres of park land on a daily basis.

  6
 Park Facility Maintenance
 Our Parks Facility Maintenance division, along with Grounds Maintenance, helped plan
 and set up, the Earth Day. We also maintained the area clean throughout the event
 with great success.

 Due to the high use of SG Park, Staff continues to do a third daily inspection and
 cleaning, in the late afternoon to our outdoor restrooms.

 The Parks Facility Maintenance Division has purchased two new pieces of equipment
 for cleaning efficiency. The first is a pressure washer for exterior cleaning of the
 sidewalks around the Parks Buildings. The second is a ride-on auto scrubber for floor
 maintenance, this machine cleans and polishes the floors.

 We have continued the use of Electrostatic Disinfecting Equipment for more coverage in
 our cleaning and disinfecting efforts for both indoor and outdoor restroom facilities,
 along with a pressure washing program. These disinfecting and cleaning tools will allow
 us to use them consecutively, giving us more cleaning coverage. Set ups for all events
 require us to disinfect all tables, chairs, door handles, and A/V equipment.

 We are in full operation with classes, as well as private rentals, picnics, sports activities,
 and service clubs events. We continue to host several food giveaways for the
 community at two locations, one at Circle Park and one at Hollydale Regional Park.

 The Community Service Worker program continues; we are still limiting intake to 15
 people maximum per day for staff safety.

 Parks continue to be open for events, classes, picnics, and sports activities. Although
 pandemic mandates have been lifted, we remain vigilant in changes from local, state,
 and federal government when addressing the ongoing challenges with restroom
 cleanliness with a weekly restroom disinfecting program to mitigate the spread of
 COVID-19. This entails the use of the C3 Machine to apply the disinfectants and
 cleaners. Once the product is sprayed, staff scrubs floors, walls, and fixtures to insure
 thoroughness.
